description:
Make `jit worktree info` take its branch from the git module's head lookup instead of its own `git rev-parse`.

## Background

- `execute_worktree_info` (`crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs:169-189`) calls the file's own `get_current_branch` (`crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs:46-63`), which runs `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in the worktree root. When git fails it reports "Failed to get current git branch. Are you in a git repository?" followed by git's stderr, which the CLI reports as `WORKTREE_INFO_ERROR` with exit 1.
- Through the module, a missing checkout starts no process and an unborn branch is `head() == Ok(None)`, so neither case has stderr to quote.
- The branch feeds the worktree identity load and the reported entry.
- CLI tests: `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/worktree_cli_tests.rs:195` onwards; unit test `crates/jit/src/commands/worktree.rs:489`.
- Kept as one change for a build reason: the file's `get_current_branch` is private, and an uncalled private function fails the zero-warning build.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `jit worktree info` takes its branch from the head lookup of the paths' git checkout, rendered as the branch name or `HEAD` when detached. The file's `get_current_branch` no longer exists.
- [hard] REQ-02: Without a git checkout the command fails with "jit worktree info requires a git repository", and on an unborn branch with "the current branch has no commits yet; make a first commit"; both report `WORKTREE_INFO_ERROR` with exit 1. CLI tests assert both, and they fail on today's message.
- [hard] REQ-03: The existing worktree info tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: the two failure messages name the requirement and no longer quote git's stderr; the code and exit status are unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Worktree info reads its branch through the module
